messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 2031526789 - HIGH_LATENCY detected in channel=streaming-runtime region=us-west1 p95 and p99 breach. Pager duty runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-latency>
alex: seeing large tail. p95 ~2.3s (normally 220ms), p99 ~8.7s. Streaming stalls flagged in trace groups 'stream-token' around token index ~120. Cache hitrate for prefix cache dropped from 84% -> 9% after midnight deploy.
mira: confirmed. correlated with prefix-hash change rolled at 02:07. lots of cache invalidations. heap of KV misses and paging to remote store.
jordan: stack traces show async fetches blocking tx path -> paging. eviction spikes too.
samir: exact symptoms: streaming sessions stall while waiting for kv fetch, then request queues up and hits tail latency threshold. repro with loadtest: reproduce quickly.
eng-runtime: log snippet:
```text
[streaming] pref_lookup miss key=pf:abcd1234 -> fetch remote (220ms)
[cache] evict rate=1200/s after rollout
[latency] p99=8700ms
```
alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back prefix-hash feature-flag 2) increase prefixcache TTL 3) enable compatibility-mode that accepts old hashes 4) route a portion of traffic to older cluster copy.
mira: rolling feature-flag back now. @ops_oncall can you confirm rollout command? I'll also trigger warmup script for hot prefixes.
ops_oncall: doing rollback: `infra featureflag set prefix-hash-v2 false --env prod --region us-west1` — applying.
incident-bot: Deploybot: rollback triggered by ops_oncall at 2031527590. Rolling back service: streaming-runtime-v2 -> streaming-runtime-v1. See <https://redwood.internal/deploys/2031527590>
alex: after rollback p95 dropped to 410ms within ~4m, p99 down to 1200ms but still above target. hitrate climbed to 56% (warmup in progress).
samir: note: some prefixes have TTL=0 for safety; we need to bump to 15m to avoid immediate evictions. doing: `kvctl set-ttl prefix-cache 900s`
eng-runtime: ran warmup: `scripts/warmup_prefixes.sh --top 5000 --region us-west1` - warmup hitrate improved local metrics.
jordan: still seeing intermittent stalls tied to long-running paging ops during warmup window. we should burst additional capacity for remote store to reduce fetch latencies.
mira: increased remote-store throughput for us-west1 by +30% (config change done). expect fetch latency drop.
ops_oncall: traffic routing change applied: 15% -> older cluster (low-cost fallback) until full stabilization. watchers: @alex @mira @jordan
alex: customer impact estimate: ~3% of requests experienced >5s latency for ~22 minutes; several timeouts observed from high-volume tenants (ids redacted). No data loss. Flagging for SLO breach at p99 window.
incident-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV3. Recording outage window 2031526789 - 2031528420 (mitigation in progress).
mira: preparing handoff notes for next oncall. key follow-ups: postmortem to include canary/rollout gating, prefix compatibility shim, validated warmup for new hash scheme, improved preflight for eviction pressure.
jordan: creating ticket: INC-2031529 - prefix-hash rollout regressions + cache-miss storm. Assign eng-runtime, infra, and sres. Link: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2031529>
ops_oncall: handing over to night oncall @nina at 2031531400. Nina — please monitor p95/p99 and confirm remote-store is still at scaled throughput. rollback remains in place; do NOT re-enable prefix-hash flag until postmortem and canary adjustments.
nina: acked. I'll take it from here and will post a short status at start of shift. will check client-facing comms with support.
alex: tl;dr: prefix-hash change caused keyspace incompatibilities -> mass cache misses -> remote paging -> streaming tail spikes. mitigations: rollback flag, warmup, increased remote throughput, route partial traffic to fallback cluster. follow-ups: compatibility shim, safer rollout gating, pre-warm scripts in CI.
incident-bot: Incident 2031526789 - mitigation in place. Next steps: schedule postmortem within 72h. Assigned INC-2031529. ":thumbsup:"
